3: > Implementation contract for `web/`. This document is the single source of truth for the Vigil
4: > web client. It supersedes `web/design.md`, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-01-web-ui-design.md`,
5: > and the earlier draft of this file.
6: 
7: Design intent: an ultra-clean, comforting, engaging surface. It rejects DevOps terminal
8: aesthetics and generic assistant slop in favour of the atmospheric calm of Google DeepMind, the
9: tactile ergonomics of Apple, and the warm, pillowy friendliness of Hark.
10: 
11: ---
12: 
13: ## 1. Product Surfaces
14: 
15: Vigil is a proactive, self-hostable personal AI assistant. The web client has three surfaces and
16: one gate:
17: 
18: | Route | Surface | Purpose |
19: |---|---|---|
20: | `/pair` | Gate | Device pairing. Renders before the app shell when no token exists. |
21: | `/` | Home | Proactive briefing: action cards, the approval queue, and what Vigil is watching. |
22: | `/chat` | Chat | Direct conversational canvas with streaming responses. |
23: | `/chat/:sessionId` | Chat | Deep link into a specific session. |
24: | `/settings` | Settings | Route-backed frosted sheet over the current surface. |
25: 
26: There is **no top navbar**. The top of the viewport stays airy. The only persistent brand element
27: is a discrete `Vigil` mark with an inline SVG spark in the upper-left margin.
28: 
29: Settings is a **route**, rendered as an intercepting sheet over the surface you came from. It is
30: not local state. This gives deep links, working browser back, and shareable URLs.
31: 
32: ---
33: 
34: ## 2. Stack Decision
35: 
36: **Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 + lucide-react.**
37: 
38: Rejected Next.js App Router. Rationale: this is a single-user authenticated client with no SEO
39: surface and no server rendering requirement. Streaming responses need custom request headers
40: (bearer token), which is straightforward in a SPA and awkward through an edge route handler. Vite
41: keeps the mental model small: one origin, one build, one `index.html`.
42: 
43: Routing: `react-router-dom` v7 in declarative mode.
44: 
45: State: `zustand` for cross-surface state (session, theme, connection health), `@tanstack/react-query`
46: for server cache and polling. No Redux, no context soup.
47: 
48: Animation: CSS only, using a spring-approximating `linear()` easing (section 6). No Framer Motion
49: in v1. If a component genuinely needs layout animation later, that is a scoped addition, not a
50: default.
51:

54: ## 3. Backend Contract
55: 
56: The web client is built against `backend/src/modules/*` as it actually exists. Do not invent types.
57: 
58: ### 3.1 Authentication
59: 
60: | Call | Shape |
61: |---|---|
62: | `POST /api/v1/auth/pair` | `{pairing_code: "VIG-XXXXXX", device_name: string}` returns `{device_token: "vgt_...", device_id, device_name}` |
63: | `GET /api/v1/auth/me` | `Authorization: Bearer vgt_...` returns `{device_id, device_name, created_at, last_seen_at}` |
64: | `POST /api/v1/auth/revoke` | invalidates the current device token |
65: 
66: The pairing code is printed as an ASCII QR on backend boot. The web client accepts it as text or
67: scans it.
68: 
69: ### 3.2 Cards (the real schema)
70: 
71: `CardResponse` from `backend/src/modules/cards/data.py`:
72: 
73: ```ts
74: type Urgency = 'critical' | 'high' | 'medium' | 'low';
75: type CardStatus = 'new' | 'seen' | 'in_progress' | 'awaiting_approval' | 'done' | 'dismissed' | 'expired';
76: 
77: interface CardAction {
78:   id: string;
79:   label: string;
80:   action_type: 'run' | 'dismiss' | 'reply' | string;
81:   payload: Record<string, unknown>;
82: }
83: 
84: interface Card {
85:   id: string;
86:   user_id: string;
87:   item_id: string | null;
88:   thread_id: string | null;
89:   type: string;              // 'email' | 'calendar' | 'alert'
90:   urgency: Urgency;
91:   title: string;
92:   summary: string | null;
93:   due_at: string | null;     // ISO datetime
94:   status: CardStatus;
95:   actions: CardAction[];
96:   feedback: string | null;
97:   created_at: string;
98:   updated_at: string;
99: }
100: ```
101: 
102: Card list responses are `{items, total, limit, offset}`.
103: 
104: There is no `ACTION READY` / `GENTLE REMINDER` / `PRE-CONFIGURED ROUTINE` taxonomy. Those were
105: invented and have no backend entity. Card visual affordances derive from the real fields:
106: 
107: | Field | Renders as |
108: |---|---|
109: | `type` | Leading lucide icon: `Mail`, `Calendar`, `TriangleAlert`. Unknown types fall back to `Circle`. |
110: | `urgency` | A 3px leading rail on the card, plus a dot for `critical`. Not a badge, not a colour wash. `critical`/`high` use accent, `medium`/`low` stay neutral. |
111: | `status` | Trailing state chip. Only `awaiting_approval` earns a filled accent chip, because it is the one status where the user is the blocker. |
112: | `due_at` | Relative time (`in 2h`, `overdue 40m`), computed client-side, `title` attribute holds the absolute timestamp. |
113: | `actions[]` | Buttons, rendered in server order. Index 0 is primary. |
114: 
115: ### 3.3 Card actions are server-driven
116: 
117: The client never decides what a card's buttons are. Rules:
118: 
119: - Render `card.actions` in order. Never hard-code "Review & Send" or "Dismiss".
120: - Dispatch on `action_type`:
121: 
122: | `action_type` | Client behaviour |
123: |---|---|
124: | `run` | `POST /api/v1/runs` with `{...payload, card_id}`, then navigate to the run's progress view |
125: | `dismiss` | `POST /api/v1/cards/{id}/dismiss`, optimistic removal |
126: | `reply` | Navigate to `/chat` with the composer seeded from `payload` |
127: | anything else | Render as a disabled ghost button so new server action types degrade instead of crashing |
128: 
129: `POST /api/v1/cards/{id}/feedback` takes `{feedback: 'useful' | 'not_useful' | 'dismissed' | 'spam', note?}`.
130: That is telemetry, not authorisation. It belongs behind an overflow menu, never as the primary button.
131: 
132: ### 3.4 Approvals are a separate module
133: 
134: Authorisation lives in `approvals`, not `cards`:
135: 
136: | Call | Shape |
137: |---|---|
138: | `GET /api/v1/approvals` | pending approvals |
139: | `GET /api/v1/approvals/{approval_id}` | one approval with its preview |
140: | `POST /api/v1/approvals/{approval_id}/decision` | body `{decision: "approved" | "rejected", decision_note?}`, returns `{approval_id, status, run_id, resumed}` |
141: 
142: `RunCreateRequest` requires `config_id`, so the card's `run` payload must carry one. The client
143: never invents a `config_id`: if the payload lacks it the backend rejects the request and the UI
144: surfaces that message.
145: 
146: A card in `awaiting_approval` has a linked approval record. The card cannot resolve itself. The
147: UI fetches the approval, shows the preview, posts the decision to `/approvals/{id}/decision`, and
148: lets the card transition on the next poll or refetch.

316: ## 6. Geometry and Motion
317: 
318: ### 6.1 Geometry
319: 
320: - Cards: `border-radius: var(--r-card)` (28px).
321: - Nested children use `var(--r-inner)`, the outer radius minus the padding, so curves stay
322:   concentric. Never nest two 28px radii.
323: - Controls: `var(--r-control)`. Pills, docks, avatars: `var(--r-pill)`.
324: - Ambient shadows only. No hard 1px borders on cards. The hairline is a subtle inset highlight.
325: 
326: ### 6.2 Motion, one primitive
327: 
328: **`--ease-spring` is the only easing in the application.** It is a CSS `linear()` approximation of a
329: spring at stiffness 400, damping 30, mass 1 (damping ratio 0.75, roughly 2.8 percent overshoot).
330: 
331: Do not add `cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1)`. It is monotonic with no overshoot and will not match
332: spring-driven components, which is exactly the inconsistency this section exists to prevent.
333: 
334: Durations: `--dur-fast` for hover and press, `--dur-base` for surface transitions, `--dur-slow` for
335: the settings sheet. Animate transforms and opacity only. Never animate `height`, `width`, `top`, or
336: `filter`.
337: 
338: All of it sits behind `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`. Under `reduce`, transitions
339: collapse to `1ms` and the ambient background stops drifting entirely.

398: ## 9. The Pairing Gate (`/pair`)
399: 
400: The app shell must never render unauthenticated. Routing rule:
401: 
402: ```
403: no token in memory  ->  redirect to /pair, preserving the intended destination
404: token present       ->  proceed
405: 401 from any call   ->  clear token, redirect to /pair, do not loop
406: ```
407: 
408: `/pair` is its own blank surface: ambient background, brand mark, and one card containing:
409: 
410: - A 6-character code input, auto-uppercasing and formatting to `VIG-XXXXXX` as the user types.
411: - A "Scan QR" affordance opening the device camera (`BarcodeDetector` where available, a clear
412:   fallback message where not).
413: - A device name field, defaulted from the user agent platform.
414: - Submit posts to `/auth/pair`, stores the token, then routes to `/`.
415: 
416: Errors: an unrecognised code (401) shows "That code was not recognised. It expires 10 minutes after
417: boot." Never show a raw backend error string on this surface.
418: 
419: Token storage: **in memory for the session, persisted in IndexedDB** so a reload does not force
420: re-pairing. Never `localStorage`, never a query string, never a cookie in v1. `POST /auth/revoke`
421: deletes the record.
